review:
The EBF series is one that's near and dear to my heart, as I grew up playing 3 and 4 when I was a kid
EBF5 is their most expanded, well polished, incredibly balanced and content dense of all of them, and that alone is a feat in it of itself

For anyone unfamiliar with the series, EBF5 although its humble origins as a flash game is the best ever RPG someone could think of as of traditional RPGs in the current day and age; if you're a fan of turn based, classical RPGs, this one is the apex of them all, as besides not being dated as most are nowadadys either visually or mechanically, it is throughout an amazing experience and even enjoyable to 100%. The game I would compare it best to would be Octopath traveller, and where it shines in its incredible storywriting and artistic detail, EBF5 has its charm and highly in-depth combat, which is simple yet vast once thoroughly applied, and the game makes use of it as best as possible.

This game genuinely is a work of art and one of the few games out there which personally encapsulate the essence of a videogame through and through; a labour of love and hard effort made to be enjoyed.

I would like to say that I've paid attention to Matt's games since Epic Battle Fantasy 2 first released on Kongregate, and I want to avoid pitting my nostalgic lens on this game because- for the record- EBF3 and 4 were the games that really introduced me to JRPGs. I've played this game both on my phone and my computer, that's how much I liked it.

I really like this game. The unique gimmick of a non-existent MP bar is really something I don't see very often, and this creates a really interesting combo system, especially because there's no initiative system; that is, your characters almost ALWAYS act first in the order of sequence they are assigned in.

This means that you can basically set up an optimal combo right from the get-go. The skill tree system is pretty simple too, learn skills, upgrade them as you obtain BP from fights. The grinding itself is very reminiscent of old RPG games, it takes a bit of time and is a slog, but it's alright. Most of this game is pretty easy to get through, but will test your knowledge on skill relationships and combos. 

It's pretty sick; every character feels defined to their given purpose and the fact that two party members can be put on reserve but can also be affected by skills makes the combat system shine quite a bit.

The story itself is largely simplistic in nature. I never liked that EBF5 was effectively a retcon and kind of reset everyone's relationships, but I got over it; the dialogue is quirky and very much the dialogue expected in the late 2010s, and it's not like the lore was incredibly extensive. I always liked Natalie and Anna, but Lance and Matt's chemistry was unparalleled...That and Natalie is just very cute in general. 

The fan works room was always my favorite to go through; I really enjoyed seeing the passion people had for this franchise.

I think the UI is pretty dated now that we're in 2026. The grind is a hassle, and I won't speak about some of the bosses' egregious health bars. This is the kind of game you play like a marathon, so I don't recommend blasting through it or you'll get burnt out.

There's quite a bit of side content; seriously, there's a lot. There's really no other games that put forth this kind of effort. Maybe Clair Obscur?

I recommend this game. It's the kind of creativity you don't really see outside of Newgrounds. I think Matt put a lot of passion into this game and this franchise; and he still makes games to this day! He seems like a good guy and I look forward to seeing future products by him.

A great but admittedly somewhat tedious RPG. 

The main focus here is on its gameplay, story is pretty basic and dialogue between characters (as well as flavor text) helps the overall pacing from the constant and often long battles. 

On that topic, the combat system is pretty interesting, you don't have the usual MP bar, instead some skills have cooldowns. You can also change your equipment mid-fight which is incredibly useful when facing off against various waves of enemies. Unfortunately some characters are professional bench warmers until the late game. If you find a team that works it can carry you throughout 90% of the game until you hit the endgame content.

My main complaint is that sometimes the battles can really drag on, usually due to some enemies' incredibly high HP bar. It's an interesting challenge, having to not only make use of status ailments but summons as well, however by the late game these types of fights just grew more tedious. 

As for the summoning mechanic, it's essentially a monster catching gimmick that can completely break the game. Some of them are absolutely overpowered while others are made completely useless by the equipment your characters can have. 

Visually the game's artstyle is very charming, reminiscent of early newgrounds as well as its writing. The music is absolutely amazing, each track just makes itself very different from each other. 

There's also a lot, and I mean A LOT of side content. I'm still deciding on wether or not to actually tackle the 100%, but until then, I heavily reccomend playing this rpg.
